binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          # gh-1522: the committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
          # stamp the PR bundle's version.txt from git describe (short sha
          # on shallow checkouts) so `fa --version` stays meaningful.
          version=$(git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0.0-dev)
          version="${version#v}"
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.

name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight; gh-1537
# retired the post-merge main ci run).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version

          # ~/bin/ci-sign can never drift from the reviewed source.
          # gh-1954: install(1) does not create parent directories —
          # on a fresh runner $HOME/bin does not exist (run 40822964468,
          # "install: invalid target .../bin/ci-sign: No such file").
          mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"

              TAG="v0.0.1"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stage the publishable package into a target directory (issue #597).
#
# `dart publish` packs everything under the repo root that isn't
# gitignored — and the root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the
# pub package (flutter_app with its 57 MB wasm toolchain, yoclip media,
# browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs, packages/*). That
# blew the archive past pub.dev's hard 100 MB cap (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB).
#
# The staged copy carries the package surface (~32 MB) plus the two PATH
# dev-dependencies (packages/fa_llm_mock, vendored vendor/xterm —
# accepted by pub.dev since v0.1.369). pubspec_overrides.yaml (the
# local-only dart_tui vendor pin, "never ships to pub.dev" by its own
# comment) must NOT enter the stage: version solving would re-pin the
# path dep and fail (the v0.1.407 failure, exit 66).
#
# Usage: stage_publish_package.sh <target-dir> [version]
#   version (gh-1522, optional) — the release version WITHOUT the leading v;
#   when given, the staged pubspec/CHANGELOG are stamped from the tag via
#   scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh (the repo files carry the 0.0.0-dev
#   placeholder and are never mutated). The publish job passes
#   "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" so the staged version always equals the tag.
# Exits non-zero (with ::error) when the staged tree exceeds the guard.
# The repo root hosts sub-projects that are NOT part of the pub package
# (flutter_app, yoclip, browser_ext, office_addin, vendored forks, docs)
# — `dart publish` packs everything under the root that isn't gitignored
# (v0.1.406: 100.4 MB, over pub.dev's hard cap). Stage the package
# surface instead. PATH dev-deps of the core pubspec must resolve inside
# the stage (#584, `dart pub get` exit 66 on v0.1.407): their subtrees
# are included BEFORE the parent excludes, and the parent excludes are
# child-scoped (vendor/*) — excluding the parent dir itself would prune
# the subtree before the includes are ever consulted.
# pubspec_overrides.yaml is the workspace-only dart_tui pin (never
# published, see its header); shipped into the stage it re-dangles
# dart_tui onto the excluded vendor dir.
set -euo pipefail

target="${1:?usage: stage_publish_package.sh <target-dir>}"
repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

mkdir -p "$target"
# Root-scoped excludes are ANCHORED: rsync matches an unanchored name
# against the basename at ANY depth — `memory` also pruned lib/src/memory/,
# shipping v0.1.411 with broken memory imports (issue #613). build/ and
# .dart_tool stay unanchored: build artifacts may appear at any depth and
# never belong in the stage.
# gh-1452: /CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (the lossless trimmed tail of CHANGELOG.md)
# has no consumer in the pub package — GitHub carries the history. It is
# excluded below; must mirror /CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md in .pubignore (guarded
# by test/publish_staging_test.dart).
rsync -a "$repo_root"/ "$target"/ \
  --include 'vendor/xterm/' --include 'vendor/xterm/**' \
  --include 'packages/fa_llm_mock/' --include 'packages/fa_llm_mock/**' \
  --exclude '/.git' --exclude '/.github' --exclude '/.worktrees' \
  --exclude '/flutter_app' --exclude '/browser_ext' \
  --exclude '/office_addin' --exclude '/yoclip' \
  --exclude 'vendor/*' --exclude '/docs' --exclude '/fa-local' \
  --exclude 'packages/*' \
  --exclude '/pubspec_overrides.yaml' \
  --exclude '/CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md' \

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the transport diagnostic renders a literal `null` in production — the shipped runner discards stderr**

`_faClipFlavorBytes` reads `result.stderr` to build the AC5 «name the transport» diagnostic:

```dart
final stderr = result.stderr;
final detail = stderr is List<int>
    ? utf8.decode(stderr, allowMalformed: true).trim()
    : '$stderr'.trim();
throw StateError(
  'fa-clip $flavor failed (exit ${result.exitCode})'
  '${detail.isEmpty ? '' : ': $detail'}',
);
```

But the production runner this always flows through — `_runBinaryProcess` (same file, line ~71) — returns **`stderr: null`** by contract:

```dart
// stderr is drained and discarded (exit codes carry failures).
return ProcessResult(process.pid, exitCode, stdout.toBytes(), null);
```

So every real quarantined/crashed/wrong-ABI helper produces:

```
pasteboard read failed: Bad state: fa-clip png failed (exit -9): null
```

…where the helper's stderr message («Killed: 9») should be. `'$stderr'` on a null is the string `"null"`, so `detail.isEmpty` never fires either — the diagnostic quality that AC5 exists for is silently lost.

The new tests don't catch this because the scripted runners hand back a **String** stderr (`ProcessResult(1, 1, <int>[], 'Killed: 9')`) — the production branch (`null`) is never exercised.

Minimal fix (keeps the runner contract untouched):

```dart
final detail = stderr is List<int>
    ? utf8.decode(stderr, allowMalformed: true).trim()
    : stderr == null
        ? ''
        : '$stderr'.trim();
```

Alternatively fold stderr into bytes in `_runBinaryProcess` (nothing else consumes it, and `boundedPasteboardWait` already drains it). Either way, please add one test whose runner mirrors the shipped shape (`stderr: null`) to pin the rendered message.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: PR CI never compiles `fa-clip` — the swiftc invocation is first exercised when cutting a real release**

This step lives in the ci.yml **`binaries`** job, whose gate (ci.yml ~4006-4010) runs it only on **tag pushes / `release` events**; the twin step in `build-macos.yml` is in a **`workflow_dispatch`-only** workflow (its `on:` block has no push/PR triggers). The PR-time binary gate, **`binaries-pr`** (ci.yml ~4796), builds the *same* macOS matrix legs (macos-latest arm64 + macos-15-intel x64) but was **not** given a fa-clip step.

Consequences:

- Per AGENTS.md, every push to `main` cuts an annotated tag via `scripts/auto_release.sh` — i.e. the very first fa-clip release build happens on the first automated post-merge release. A toolchain failure there breaks a real release, not a PR.
- The specific risk worth smoking out: `scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` pins `-target arm64-apple-macos10.13`, but arm64 macOS slices have a minimum deployment target of 11.0 — toolchains typically bump/warn rather than fail, but that behavior (and swiftc availability on the `macos-15-intel` x64 leg) is exactly the kind of thing only a real macOS build proves.

Please do one of:

1. Dispatch `build-macos` with `create_release=false` against this branch (or right after merge) and confirm **both** arch legs compile + `test -x` the helper; or
2. Mirror this build step into the `binaries-pr` macOS legs so every PR that touches the helper (or the build script) compiles it, matching the existing «compiles is not works» smoke discipline (gh-1280 NG2).

Option 2 is the durable fix; option 1 is the minimum verification for this PR.

💡 **SUGGESTION: helper overwrite is non-atomic and a stale helper is never cleaned up**

Two small robustness gaps in `copyBundleClipboardHelper`, both contrasted with how the main binary is already handled:

1. **Non-atomic overwrite.** The fa binary swap goes through `_atomicSwap` (staging file + rename), so a crash mid-update can never leave a half-written binary. The helper is truncated in place:

```dart
await helperTarget.writeAsBytes(src.readAsBytesSync());
```

A crash/disk-full mid-write leaves a corrupt `fa-clip` beside a freshly swapped binary — recoverable only by reinstall (it degrades per AC5, so this is polish, not a bug). Reusing `_atomicSwap` would give the helper the same guarantee for free.

2. **Stale helper retention.** When the new bundle has **no** `bin/fa-clip` (older-release rollback is the doc'd shape), a previously installed `fa-clip` stays beside the binary and the new reader keeps executing it. With today's stable protocol that's harmless, but the first future protocol change turns «no-op on helper-less bundles» into «silently runs a mismatched protocol». Consider deleting a pre-existing `$installDir/fa-clip` when the bundle lacks one — that also makes the doc comment's AC5 claim literally true.

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the documented `exit 1` contract is unreachable — drop it or emit it**

The header pins a four-way exit contract:

```
//   exit 2  — the pasteboard holds no data of the requested flavor
//   exit 1  — the pasteboard could not be read (message on stderr)
```

…but no code path can produce `exit 1`: the only fallible call, `NSPasteboard.general.data(forType:)`, is non-throwing and maps `nil` → `exit(2)` («flavor absent»). The Dart side (`_faClipFlavorBytes`) accordingly treats only `0`/`2` as fall-through and everything else — including a hypothetical 1 — as a transport failure.

Since the helper's contract is load-bearing (it is grep-gated and protocol-tested), keep the header honest: either delete the `exit 1` line, or actually produce it (e.g. wrap the read and report a genuinely failed pasteboard access distinctly from flavor-absent) so a real pasteboard-server error doesn't masquerade as «no such flavor».

💡 **SUGGESTION: gitignore the script's default output — it lands inside the tracked tree *and* the pub stage**

```bash
OUT="${1:-$REPO_ROOT/tools/fa-clip/fa-clip}"
```

Every caller passes an explicit OUT (CI: `build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip`, `install_local.sh`: `$INSTALL_DIR/fa-clip`), but a bare `bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh` — the path a developer will most naturally try — drops a Mach-O binary at `tools/fa-clip/fa-clip`, and `.gitignore` has no entry for it. Two knock-on effects:

- `git status` noise in the tracked tree;
- `/tools/` is **not** excluded by `.pubignore` / `scripts/stage_publish_package.sh` (that's why `tools/crap_top.sh` ships today), so a locally built binary present at pack/stage time would ride the pub.dev payload as dead weight.

One `.gitignore` line fixes both:

```
/tools/fa-clip/fa-clip
```

(Or flip the default OUT outside the repo tree, e.g. `build/fa-clip`.)
